content.value_statement: AI agents can collide when they change the same repository. This skill describes coordinated version control, learning trajectories, and conflict-aware repository work.
actual_capabilities: Explains installation and basic use of the agentic-jujutsu package.
Documents JjWrapper operations for status, commits, logs, diffs, branches, and rebases.
Shows how to record learning trajectories with success scores and critiques.
Describes suggestion, pattern discovery, statistics, and trajectory query APIs.
Provides examples for multi-agent review, deployment, merges, and task loops.
Lists validation rules for task descriptions, scores, operations, and context values.
limitations: The skill is documentation-focused and depends on the external package for behavior.
Performance and success-rate claims come from the source documentation and need independent validation.
Users must review repository-changing commands before running them.
The skill does not provide a complete implementation inside the skill directory.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Concurrent AI Changes
use_cases.description: Plan repository work when several AI agents create commits or branches at the same time.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads managing AI coding agents

use_cases.title: Record Learning From Repository Work
use_cases.description: Track task trajectories, outcomes, and critiques so later agents can reuse successful patterns.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agentic Version Control APIs
use_cases.description: Review documented methods for operations, statistics, pattern discovery, and quantum fingerprint support.
use_cases.target_user: Tooling architects assessing AI development infrastructure

prompt_templates.title: Summarize The Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview before trying the package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agentic-jujutsu to explain the basic workflow for one AI agent making repository changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Agent Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate several agents on related code changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agentic-jujutsu to plan how three AI agents should create branches, record trajectories, and avoid conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Design Learning Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve future repository tasks from completed work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agentic-jujutsu to design a trajectory recording process with success scores, critiques, and pattern review.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Advanced Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agentic-jujutsu to review a proposed integration with concurrent agents, command execution, encryption, and rollback handling.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe workflow for two agents changing one repository.
output_examples.output: A branch and trajectory plan that separates each agent task, records outcomes, and checks conflicts before integration.

output_examples.input: Explain why suggestions have low confidence.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis that points to limited trajectory history and recommends recording several successful and failed examples.

output_examples.input: Review a deployment workflow that uses learned operations.
output_examples.output: A concise review of tracking points, outcome scoring, validation checks, and command approval steps.

best_practices: Use clear task descriptions so trajectory records are searchable and reusable.
Record both successful and failed outcomes with honest success scores.
Review command examples before applying them to an active repository.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated suggestions as approval to run repository-changing commands.
Do not record vague tasks because they reduce learning quality.
Do not rely on performance claims without testing them in your own workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users understand Agentic Jujutsu workflows for AI-assisted version control and learning from repository operations.

faq.question: Does the skill include executable source code?
faq.answer: No. The scanned skill is a documentation file that references an external package and its APIs.

faq.question: Can it coordinate multiple AI agents?
faq.answer: The documentation describes patterns for concurrent agents, branch work, trajectory tracking, and shared learning.

faq.question: Does it automatically run commands?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the skill file. Users must decide whether to run the documented package commands.

faq.question: Why does it mention quantum security?
faq.answer: The documentation describes SHA3 fingerprinting and encryption-related APIs from the package.

faq.question: What should users verify before adoption?
faq.answer: Users should inspect the external package, test repository behavior, and confirm claims in a safe environment.
